name: Central Andean highland peoples (Chanka, Huanca and other Quechua groups)
summary: The Quechua-speaking highland groups of central Peru that stood outside the Inca heartland before the 15th-century Inca expansion, notably the Chanka and the Huanca; a stub to be improved.

location.value: The central Peruvian highlands: the Chanka in the Huancavelica, Ayacucho and Apurímac regions (capital at Sondor near Andahuaylas), and the Huanca in the Mantaro Valley of Junín.
location.source: Wikipedia: Quechua people (search excerpt); Wikipedia: Huanca (search excerpt); Huillca Expedition: history of the Chankas (search excerpt)

governmentType.value: Separate ethnic groups, not one state; the Chanka are described as a powerful ethnic group from the Andahuaylas region. They sat alongside the Huancas and the Collas as the main late-intermediate groups compared with the Inca.
governmentType.source: Ossio, El Tahuantinsuyo de los Incas (search excerpt)

majorWars.value: The Great Inca-Chanka War is dated to about 1438, when the Chanka are said to have marched on Cusco with a force of over 40,000; the Huanca were conquered by Pachacuti in the 15th century after fierce fighting and then supplied soldiers for Inca campaigns in Quito.
majorWars.source: Huillca Expedition: history of the Chankas (search excerpt); Wikipedia: Huanca (search excerpt)

territoryChange.value: Both were absorbed into Tawantinsuyu (the Inca Empire) during the 15th century.
territoryChange.source: Huillca Expedition: history of the Chankas (search excerpt); Wikipedia: Huanca (search excerpt)

languageWriting.value: Both spoke Quechua. The Huanca varieties differ significantly from the Cusco Quechua of the Incas, and the Huanca spoke Quechua before the Incas did.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Quechua people (search excerpt); Wikipedia: Huanca (search excerpt)

sharedIdentity.value: 'Quechua people' means any of the indigenous peoples who speak Quechua languages; the dialects differ so much that some are not mutually intelligible.

riseSignals.value: Chanka culture is believed to have developed between the 12th and 15th centuries, before the Inca expansion.
riseSignals.source: Huillca Expedition: history of the Chankas (search excerpt)

sources.value: Search excerpts only (no full page read): Wikipedia mirrors on Quechua people and Huanca, the Huillca Expedition blog on the Chankas, and a book excerpt by Ossio; 17 Nov 2026. The blog is a tourism site and the date 1438 is not checked against an academic source.

overallCertainty.value: Weak: a stub built from excerpts. Details of the Inca-Chanka war come from later Spanish and Inca-era chronicles.
overallCertainty.source: Huillca Expedition: history of the Chankas (search excerpt)
